candidates.description: Presence of the activating KRAS G12C missense mutation in the tumor.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify mentions of 'KRAS G12C' or 'c.34G>T (p.G12C)' in the genomic findings section.
candidates.measurement_definition: Positive if the KRAS c.34G>T (p.G12C) mutation is detected via NGS; negative if KRAS is wild-type or harbors a different mutation.
candidates.name: KRAS G12C mutation status
candidates.uncertainty: Whether the specific variant allele frequency (VAF) of the G12C mutation influences the retrieval signal beyond its binary presence.

candidates.description: The estimated number of copies of the MET gene, used to identify MET amplification.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Search for 'MET' in the genomic findings table and extract the associated 'copy number' or 'copies' value.
candidates.measurement_definition: The numerical value of the MET gene copy number as determined by normalized read depth from NGS or qPCR.
candidates.name: MET copy number
candidates.uncertainty: Variation in thresholds for 'low-level' vs 'amplification' across different laboratory reporting standards.

limitations: Small sample size of unique patients across the provided excerpts.
Data is limited to retrospective reports with varying sequencing depths and analytical sensitivities.
Lack of consistent reporting for all variables (e.g., TMB and PD-L1 are only mentioned in a subset of cases).
summary: The evidence distinguishes between two primary genomic driver profiles in non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) adenocarcinomas: those harboring the KRAS G12C mutation (often associated with STK11 or CDKN2A loss) and those harboring EGFR exon 19 deletions (often associated with MET amplification). TP53 R273C is a common co-mutation across both groups.
